operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

responseBody.description: Newly created user profile (excluding credential data).

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Searches or lists comments attached to a specific post in the BBS platform, with support for filtering, pagination, and sorting. This operation targets the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users and visitors to explore threads and reply-chains belonging to a post.
operations.description:
This API allows users to retrieve a list of comments for a specific post, identified by 'postId'. Supports query options for filtering by author, time range, reply depth, and more—including pagination and sort order. The underlying 'comments' table returns summaries or basics details of each comment thread or reply chain, supporting threaded conversation navigation.

Both authenticated users and visitors can access this operation, but may see different levels of detail according to permissions. The endpoint is closely linked with comment creation (POST), update (PUT), and deletion (DELETE) for participation and moderation flows. Only comments belonging to the target postId are returned, supporting thread-based exploration and analysis.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

Fully aligns with the comments entity as specified in the requirements and comments table in the Prisma schema, including parent-child threading, audit, and moderation soft-delete support.

content.description:
Comment body text.

This property contains the text that will be displayed as the content of the comment. It implements the rule that each comment consists of user-written content. For example: 'I agree and here’s why...'. Referenced from the 'content' column in the Prisma comments model and per requirements in 03_data_structure_and_business_rules.md.

oneOf.description:
The ID of the parent comment for nested/threaded replies. Nullable for top-level comments (direct replies to posts).

Referenced from 'parent_id' in the comments Prisma schema. Implements thread/nesting support and conversation branching per requirements.

parent_id.description:

bbsComments.ICreate.description:
Model for creating a new comment on a post or as a reply to another comment.

Based on the requirements document and comments schema, this interface allows users to create either a top-level comment or a nested reply. Only registered users may comment. Thread assignment is supported via optional parent_id.

event.scenario: Validate fetching a single comment's full details by ID under a given post. First, create a post and add a comment to it. Retrieve the comment by its ID and verify that all expected fields (content, author, timestamps, parent information etc.) are present. Then attempt to fetch a non-existent or unrelated comment ID and verify the API returns the correct not-found or error response. Also check permission scenarios: different users accessing the same comment (public vs. restricted).
event.review: Excellent strategic breakdown covering every required aspect. The steps track the business dependencies (user ➔ post ➔ comment) and establish both positive and negative test scenarios. All required API calls and their required parameters are mapped out; the plan distinguishes user context switches and ensures that both expected and not-found/error cases are validated. All dependencies are feasible with provided API and DTOs, and the outlined stepwise process matches the scenario's requirements. Be sure to assert the type and the actual content fields for the returned comment, and to use TestValidator.error for not-found cases. Also validate that both users (author and unrelated) can access the comment.

scenario.draft: Test adding a new top-level comment to an existing post. For a successful path, create a user and a post, then submit a valid comment (non-empty content). Confirm the comment is recorded and returned with the expected metadata. For input validation, attempt comments with empty content or referencing a non-existent post and verify appropriate validation or not-found errors are returned. Also attempt to comment while unauthenticated and assert the expected permission error is returned.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

responseBody.description: Newly created user profile (excluding credential data).

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

requestBody.description: Information for the new post, including title, content, and category ID.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

Business rules ensure audit trails and uphold moderation policies. Related endpoints include comment creation, deletion, and listing under post/group context.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

event.review:
The draft documents a clear test plan that ensures the votes.getById endpoint enforces correct access control and proper error signaling for not-found resources. However, the ability to switch user roles (to authenticated User B or guest/no-auth) cannot be implemented unless explicit authentication/authorization APIs are provided by the SDK. Since the provided materials do not include any auth endpoints (register, login, token), the test cannot perform actual user switching or guest sessions, and must remain within the context of the single authenticated user. The only directly implementable negative case is fetching a non-existent vote by a valid user. Steps involving User B or guest can be described but not coded. Therefore, the implementable procedures are:
1. As the current authenticated user, create a vote (for later use).
2. As the same user, verify fetching it succeeds (optional for completeness).
3. As the same user, attempt to fetch a completely random/non-existent vote ID and confirm a not-found error. Attempting to test as a different user or guest cannot be coded and must be omitted or commented.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

Operates on 'votes' table and applies business logic: a user may vote once per target (enforced by a unique constraint), and the value must be +1 or -1. Only authenticated users can vote. The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:

Results typically return basic post details—such as title, author summary, vote tallies, timestamps—and allow users to quickly find, browse, and analyze current discussions.

If the query contains unsupported or invalid parameters, the system returns an appropriate error. This endpoint is commonly used alongside post creation (POST), update (PUT), detail view (GET), and deletion (DELETE) operations.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

This API allows the original author (or, in special cases, a moderator/administrator) to update an existing post identified by its UUID. The client supplies updated values for title, content, or other modifiable fields. The 'posts' table enforces that only the recorded author or privileged account can submit updates to a given post record.

The system maintains a history of 'updated_at' timestamps and can restrict updates to within certain time windows, as described by business requirements. Attempting to update with invalid data (missing or duplicate title, empty content, invalid references) produces an error. Related endpoints include post creation (POST), detailed retrieval (GET), and deletion (DELETE).

The API returns the updated post data upon success, immediately reflecting any changes in subsequent queries.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.scenario: Test that a user who is not the author of a post and lacks necessary privileges cannot delete the post. Attempt deletion from a different user account. Validate that the attempt is rejected due to authorization rules, the post remains in the system, and no sensitive information is leaked.
event.review:
Overall, the code achieves the business scenario of ensuring an unauthorized user can't delete another user's post. 

Strengths:
- Well-structured steps: user registration, category/post creation, privilege switch, unauthorized operation, assertion.
- Uses typia.assert and TestValidator for critical validations.
- Follows business DTO and API constraints, only using what is present in the DTO/API list.
- Documents each step and business logic clearly.
- No superfluous type bypasses: strictly type-safe.

Minor Comments:
- The simulation of switching auth context is noted in the comment, since no login API is present. In a real system, the connection would need to have user context switched; here, only API calls and types used.
- It checks for the "error is thrown" condition per scenario, but can't re-GET the post due to missing GET API; properly documents this.

Conclusion: Code is clean, type-safe, implementable, strictly aligned with available materials, and clearly explains any business/test limitations. No fictional APIs/DTOs are used.

operations.description: This operation enables privileged users (moderators, administrators) to retrieve a paginated list of all users registered on the discussion board. The returned user data includes public profile information (username, email, bio), their user role, account status, and registration metadata. Filtering and searching capabilities provide powerful moderation and community management tools, allowing admins to quickly investigate misuse, track new registrations, or query dormant/suspended accounts. Pagination parameters prevent excessive database load. The endpoint ensures security by requiring bearer authentication and restricting access to users with sufficient privileges (moderator or administrator). This operation references the users Prisma schema model, specifically all columns described (id, user_role_id, username, email, bio, status, created_at, updated_at). The response should not include password hashes. Validation includes correct filter types, secure pagination defaults, and correct authorization checks. This operation may be combined with single-user lookup or management operations for a full user administration workflow.

Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

event.scenario: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of users as a privileged moderator/administrator. Authenticate with bearer token as an admin, then use valid search and filter parameters (username substring, email domain, status) with pagination settings. Verify response includes user data (excluding sensitive fields) and pagination metadata. Ensure only matching records are returned and the system enforces pagination defaults.
event.review:
The draft implementation covers the scenario as described. It: 
- Sets up several users with varying roles, statuses, and emails
- Builds a test user pool, making sure admin and non-admin are present
- Performs a paginated, filtered search for users on username substring and email domain, plus an actual status taken from created users (since status can't be set on create)
- Asserts filter correctness, pagination, and page boundary navigation
- Optionally tests for empty result using negative filter
Type safety is preserved, and all operations use the provided DTO contracts. Auth is assumed to already exist in connection.

Areas to watch:
- Assumes role IDs are arbitrary UUIDs for test, as there is no API to fetch or create user roles. This is valid for E2E test environments.
- No way to explicitly create user with a given status; finds it from creation result (as supported in API).
- Sensitive field exclusion is handled by DTO type assertion and is properly checked.
- No explicit authentication API exists, so privileged context is simulated.
No fictional or unimplementable features included, and the test validates both positive and negative filtering/pagination cases clearly.

- Variable names are descriptive and reflect their purpose.
- Proper use of random data generation utilities.
- No use of forbidden constructs, fictional functions, or external types.

**Code Review for test_api_bbs_test_update_user_profile_as_self_with_valid_data**

1. **Compilation & Syntax**
   - Uses TypeScript strict typing for all DTO values and API responses.
   - Parameter and return types are appropriately enforced—no `any`, `as`, or suppression comments are used.
   - Utilizes the right parameter shapes and satisfies constraints for input types.
   - All SDK calls use correct parameter property names.
2. **Framework Compliance**
   - Uses only the permitted API functions from provided SDK.
   - Maintains code structure: single exported async function with proper doc string and descriptive comments.
   - Asserts all returned API objects with `typia.assert()` for type-safety.
   - API responses are not returned—only validated.
3. **Business Rule and Scenario Analysis**
   - Checks all business-relevant fields: id, username, email, bio, user_role_id, status, updated_at.
   - Uniqueness is respected via randomization (no duplicate emails/usernames).
   - Ensures new role_id is different from initial.
   - Validates that only intended changes took effect.
   - Validates time progression (`updated_at` changed).
   - Checks that unchanged status field was not modified by update.
   - Properly documents every test step with rationale.
4. **TestValidator Usage**
   - Uses `equals`, `notEquals`, and `predicate` with correct actual/expected order and curried calls.
   - Messages describe exactly what is being validated.
5. **Type Safety Enforcement**
   - All generated values, inputs, and assertions strictly match provided DTO types.
   - Satisfies-only, never uses `as any` or similar.
   - No fictional functions or DTOs are referenced.

**Suggestions**:
- If an actual list of available roles exists, consider fetching a valid one instead of generating random UUIDs. For now, a random different UUID suffices.
- No error-path testing here (since scenario is success path). If needed, could add a duplicate email/username scenario in the future.

operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

event.review:

It then attempts to soft-delete the target user's account using the permissions of the test user. Since the API/context does not offer explicit login functions or session switching, the test relies on the assumption that each operation runs in the current connection context, representing the test user. The test finally uses TestValidator.error to confirm that insufficient permission triggers the appropriate error. 

Strengths:

- Isolates non-admin, non-owner user scenario for permissions validation.
- Properly asserts output and error behavior.

Weaknesses:
- Relies on simulated role/connection switching due to the lack of explicit authentication/session APIs.
- Does not test with an actual admin (out of scope for this scenario).

Result: The logic is clear, correctly scoped, and focuses on runtime business logic error handling as required. Only actual, implementable API flows are included. Naming follows required format for integration.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

Input data includes the reply content and optional metadata (e.g., authored by user, timestamp auto-handled). The 'comments' table enforces this hierarchy and business rules such as only registered users may reply, and soft deletion logic applies. Error handling ensures the parent comment exists and is not deleted. /**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`

event.scenario: Test listing all direct replies to a valid parent comment. First, create a user and log in to obtain authentication. Create a post, then add a comment to this post. Proceed to create multiple replies to this comment using the proper threading mechanism. Then, retrieve the list of replies with various pagination and filter settings. The test must verify that only direct (not deeply nested) replies are returned, the structure matches pagination requests, and content and author data aligns with created replies. Confirm that accessing this endpoint for an existing comment that has no replies returns an empty paginated list.
event.review:
The draft implementation sets a clear step-by-step structure following the scenario and covers the full end-to-end workflow, including setup, reply threading, pagination checks, content and author validation, and negative test for empty reply list. Some improvements:
- Specify random data generation and assertion checks for each creation step.
- For reply list: collect created reply IDs and contents, and validate against API response for correct order and user/content integrity.
- For pagination, choose a reasonable direct reply count (e.g., 3), and test both default and custom (limit=2, page=2, etc.).
- For nested noise reply: validate it's excluded from direct child list.
- For empty-replies comment: assert data array is empty, pagination total 0.
Code must make all API calls per sequence, assert types (typia), and use TestValidator to check logic, not just API response shapes.

scenario.draft: Test error handling and access control when retrieving replies for a comment that has been deleted (soft-deleted). First, create a user, a category, and a post. Add a comment, then soft-delete (mark as deleted) the comment using the delete comment endpoint. Attempt to request replies for the deleted parent comment and verify that the system responds with an appropriate error or empty result, ensuring no unauthorized access or logical violation.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:

Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.

  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

responseBody.description: Data of the newly created category.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.
operations.summary: Create a new post (BBS: posts table).

requestBody.description: Information for the new post, including title, content, and category ID.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

Input data includes the reply content and optional metadata (e.g., authored by user, timestamp auto-handled). The 'comments' table enforces this hierarchy and business rules such as only registered users may reply, and soft deletion logic applies. import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.
